hook_text: Why does a winch handle not spin back and break your fingers? A toothed wheel and a tiny finger.
clip_script: Saw teeth on a wheel: a long slope, a short steep side. A pawl, a little spring-loaded arm, presses on them. Turn the wheel the free way and the slopes lift the arm: click, click, click. Try to turn it back and the arm hits a steep face and jams. Locked. That is the ratchet and pawl. It does not add force; it decides which way is allowed. Boat winch, ratchet spanner, cable tie, handbrake lever. Same trick every time. Design rule: hard steel pawl, pivoted so the load pushes it deeper in, and a release so you can unwind.
visual_style: Whiteboard wheel with saw teeth; pawl riding up slopes with click marks; reverse attempt with the pawl jammed and a red cross; quick cuts to winch, spanner, cable tie, handbrake.
mood: Snappy and mechanical, with a satisfying click.
pacing: Teeth, pawl, click click, jam, four uses, design rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make a clicking ratchet from card and a rubber band.
